module: Mark synthetic outputs and verify detection

lesson.title: Trace provenance through a product: case exercise
lesson.summary: Trace marking and detection through generation, editing, export and delivery.

prerequisites.reason: The case requires a reasoned choice of marking methods and preservation tests. The case includes modality-specific constraints and free-form text.
The learner must retain the product provider’s responsibility through upstream handoffs.
The case requires implementation evidence beyond a supplier claim.

blocks: Case: Harbour provides a generator using an external model. It delivers images and free-form text to customers. Assume its current outputs are in scope and do not qualify for an editing exception.
The supplier marks the original image using signed metadata and a watermark. Harbour's preview verifies it. That preview is one stage of the delivery path, not evidence for every later stage.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(2), 50(5)-(7); Code Section 1 Commitments 1-4
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Harbour's publishing export removes metadata. Its resizing step changes the image. The watermark detector still works on some outputs, but no representative final-file tests were retained.

Test the actual transformations and final files. A layered approach can improve resilience, but the loss of one layer requires checking whether the remaining route still satisfies the relevant qualities and Code commitments.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(2), 50(5)-(7); Code Section 1 Commitments 1-4
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Its detector sometimes mislabels authentic images. Harbour needs positive and negative test samples, relevant transformations and clear statements of the detection result's limitations.
Document effectiveness, reliability, robustness and interoperability separately. A successful detection does not prove the image's statements or depiction are true.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(2), 50(5)-(7); Code Section 1 Commitments 1-4

blocks: For free-form text, Harbour must evaluate the route suited to that format and current technical limits. It cannot copy a document-file metadata result to raw text without explaining how the delivered marking is detectable.

Retain the verified detection route and proportionate privacy/security arrangements. Preserve the distinctions between mandatory Code commitments, optional methods and the law's feasibility-sensitive test.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(2), 50(5)-(7); Code Section 1 Commitments 1-4
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: A defensible workflow record identifies who provides the system, which outputs are marked, the preservation path, compatible detection, actual tests and the correction owner.

Do not declare 'compliant' solely from a supplier signature or a visible badge. This exercise checks the current ordinary commercial workflow; it does not decide criminal-law authorisation or grandfathering dates.
